REPORT FOR ACTION 
Supplementary Report: Transit Priority Measures to 
Support the 505 Dundas 6-Minute Network 
Date: December 12, 2025 
To: City Council 
From: Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation Services 
Wards: 4 – Parkdale-High Park, 9 – Davenport, 10 – Spadina-Fort York, 13 – Toronto 
Centre 
SUMMARY 
At its meeting on November 27, 2025, Toronto East York Community Council directed 
Transportation Services to report directly to the December 16, 2025 meeting of City 
Council on proposed transit priority measures on the south side of Dundas Street West 
between Dovercourt Road and Bay Street. Staff were also directed to engage with local 
Business Improvement Areas, resident associations, the friends of Trinity Bellwoods, 
and the Trinity Bellwoods Farmers Market to review opportunities to ensure accessibility 
and report back to Toronto and East York Community Council at a future date. Staff 
have revised the original proposed transit priority measures to include the new section 
of Dundas Street West as directed. Transportation Services is recommending that City 
Council adopt the recommendation in this supplementary report along with 
Recommendations 2 and 3 from Toronto and East York Community Council. 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
The Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation Services 
recommends that: 
1. City Council delete Toronto and East York Community Council Recommendation 
1 and adopt instead the following new recommendation: 
a. City Council authorise amendments to parking and traffic regulations as 
set out in Attachment 1 to the supplementary report (December 12, 2025) 
from the Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation 
Services, to take effect from January 1, 2026.

FINANCIAL IMPACT 
Transportation Services has consulted with Toronto Parking Authority (TPA), who 
assessed that the potential financial impact of lost revenue and operating expenses will 
be approximately $506,000 in the first year and $496,000 in subsequent years (HST 
excluded). The estimated cost to implement the curbside and turning regulations is 
$156,000 (pre-HST), which will be funded from the TTC’s 2025-2034 Capital Budget 
and Plan. These costs cover all amendments in Attachment 1 to the supplementary 
report (December 12, 2025). 
DECISION HISTORY 
At its meeting on November 27, 2025, in considering “TE27.51 – Transit Priority 
Measures to Support the 505 Dundas 6-Minute Network”, Toronto and East York 
Community Council directed the General Manager, Transportation Services, in 
consultation with the Chief Executive Officer, Toronto Transit Commission to report 
directly to the December 16, 2025 meeting of City Council on proposed transit priority 
measures on the south side of Dundas Street West between Dovercourt Road and Bay 
Street. 
Agenda Item History – 2025.TE27.51 
COMMENTS 
Based on direction from Toronto East York Community Council on November 27, 2025, 
Attachment 1 to this report has been revised to include the original proposed transit 
priority measures on Dundas Street as outlined within the report dated November 10, 
2025, as well as additional proposed transit priority measures on the south side of 
Dundas Street West between Dovercourt Road and Bay Street, and the north side of 
Dundas Street West between Dovercourt Road and Ossington Avenue. Only the newly 
proposed transit priority measures will be detailed in this report, as the original transit 
priority measures have already been discussed in the report submitted on November 
10, 2025.

where new TPMs are being proposed, listed in Table 1. Three roadway characteristics 
are consistent along the corridor:

• The road is 2 lanes per direction; and 
• Streetcar tracks are present in the centre lane.

Transit Priority Measures 
The proposed transit priority measures (TPMs) were developed by focusing on parking 
and traffic regulatory prohibitions during the AM and PM peak periods on weekdays. 
These measures aim to improve the speed and reliability of the 505 Dundas streetcar in 
the peak periods. 
Stopping Restrictions 
As noted in the November 10, 2025 report for TE25.71, the changes to curbside 
regulations target sections of Dundas Street West where there are ‘No Stopping’ 
restrictions in only one peak period from Monday to Friday, on each side of the street. In 
these sections, the curbside regulations will be updated so each side of the street has 
‘No Stopping’ in both peak periods, from Monday to Friday. 
The existing and proposed ‘No Stopping’ and ‘No Parking’ restrictions have been 
provided for the newly proposed TPMs in Table 2. Detailed changes to ‘No Stopping’ 
and ‘No Parking’ restrictions can be found in Attachment 1.

Consultation 
TTC continues to consult on the project, including with the local Councillors, Deputy 
Mayor, and BIAs on the new TPMs proposed in this report. For local residents and 
businesses, mailers will be sent out to communicate the changes to the parking 
restrictions along Dundas Street. As directed by Toronto and East York Community 
Council on November 27, 2025, staff will continue to engage with resident associations, 
the Friends of Trinity Bellwoods, and the Trinity Bellwoods Farmers Market to review 
opportunities to ensure accessibility, with findings to be reported back to Toronto and 
East York Community Council in Q2 2026. 
Monitoring 
The same monitoring methodologies outlined in the November 10, 2025 report for 
TE27.51 applies to the newly proposed TPMs outlined in this report. As directed by 
Toronto and East York Community Council, on November 27, 2025, staff will report on 
the performance of the TPMs at TEYCC on May 28, 2026.
